 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Siddappa Nilishettar S/o Late Puttanashetti.

2. The brief facts of the case is that, on 11.01.2023 at about 06:45 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kunigal Police Station, the deceased Siddappa Nilshettar and Santhoshkumar were standing and conversation near Anchepalya Bus stop, N.H. 75 road at Anchepalya village, Hutridurga Hobli,
Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur SCCH - 7 3 MVC No.2938/2023 District, at that time the accused/driver drove the offending Bolero Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- AC-4485 from Kunigal side towards Nelamangala side in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life

and dashed to the pedestrian Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar who was standing and conversation with Santhoshkumar,
as a result the said Sri.Siddappa Nilishettar, fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his head and he died due to injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.
Thereafter, the informant/Santhoshkumar lodged complaint before the Kunigal police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.10/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279, 304A of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

3. It is contended that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the minor children of the deceased Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar and as on the date of the alleged accident the said deceased was aged about 45 years and doing labour work and earning income was Rs.20,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- under different head of loss of dependency, funeral and obsequies expenses, loss of filial love, loss of consortium, loss of estate.
SCCH - 7 4 MVC No.2938/2023 4.

It is contended that the accident is solely due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver/Rajkumar of the offending Bolero Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 04-AC-4485 and the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Hence,

2 both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: In pursuance of notice issued to the Respondents No.1 and 2, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte and Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioner has not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased who was tried to cross the road without observing the on coming vehicles.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.

As such SCCH - 7 5 MVC No.2938/2023 the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the deceased and further period that the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V.Act.
Hence sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of pleadings/contentions of both parties, my predecessors have framed the following issues:

2) Whether the Petitioners prove the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
3) Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs of deceased siddappa Nilishettar S/o Late Puttanashetti?
4) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?

sentences.text: The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioners.

Hence, in order to prove their case,
the Petitioner No.1 herself examined as P.W.1 and she has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in her evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.12 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of complaint dated 11.01.2023, Ex.P-3 is the true copy of the spot panchanama dated 12.01.2023, Ex.P-4 is the True copy of the spot sketch, Ex.P-5 is the true copy of the seizer mahazar dated 12.01.2023, Ex.P-6 is the true copy of Motor vehicle inspection report,

Ex.P-7 is the true copy of the inquest, Ex.P-8 is the Postmortem report, Ex.P-9 is the true copy of Charge Sheet, Ex.P-10 is the Adhar card of Petitioner No.1, Ex.P-11 is the Adhar card of Petitioner No.2, Ex.P-12 is the Adhar Card of Petitioner No.3.
SCCH - 7 9 MVC No.2938/2023 13.
In the cross-examination of PW-1, she has deposed that the deceased is her husband and father of Petitioners No.2 and 3.

Further deposed that the deceased was working in the brick factory company by name Winner burger factory and earning salary of Rs.20,000/- p.m., and she has not produced any documents to show the alleged income of her husband.
Further she denied that the deceased is aged morethan 45 years at the time of alleged accident.
Further she denied that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the deceased.
Further she denied that the deceased on conversation with his brother negligently and suddenly crossed the road with taking note of the approaching the offending vehicle.
Further she deposed that she has not received any compensation from the said factory in which the deceased was working.
Further she denied that she has not spent amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral expenditure of the deceased.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition and she has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

14. On careful reading of Ex.P6/IMV report, it specifies that the Cw.12/Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical disorders in respect of the said offending vehicle and further the said inspector SCCH - 7 10 MVC No.2938/2023 noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, front bumper bent inwards, radiator grill dislocated and front left side bonnet bent inwards, rest all the parts were intact.
15.

On going through the Ex.P-8/Postmortem report it is seen that CW.13/Doctor opined that cause of death of deceased Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar is due to shock and hemorrhages as result of injury to the head and due to injuries sustained in the alleged road traffic accident.
16.

The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and in order to prove its version the Respondent No.2 has neither stepped into the witness box nor produced documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross- examined the PW-1.

17. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint it is seen that on 11.01.2023 at about 06:45 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kunigal Police Station, the deceased Siddappa Nilishettar and first informant/Santhoshkumar were standing and conversation near Anchepalya Bus stop, N.H. 75 road Usha Nilishettar vs Nanjundappa on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91915426/

No.KA-04-AC-4485 from Kunigal side SCCH - 7 11 MVC No.2938/2023 towards Nelamangala side in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the Sri. Siddappa Nilishetta who was standing and conversation with first informant/Santhoshkumar, as a result the said Sri.Siddappa Nilishettar,
fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his head and he died due to injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.
Thereafter, the informant/Santhoshkumar lodged complaint before the Kunigal police station.
Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.10/2023 and prepared Ex.P-1/F.I.R., for the offence punishable under sections 279, 304A of IPC.
On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint, on 12-01-2023, informant/Santhoshkumar showed the place of incident to the police.

The police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar in the presence of panch witnesses i.e.
CW.2 and CW.3 and during the mahazar the police have prepared Ex.P4/spot sketch.

Admittedly,
the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar died due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to the no fault of the accused, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

On going through the prosecution papers,
FIR, mahazar, spot SCCH - 7 12 MVC No.2938/2023 sketch, IMV Report, Inquest mahazar,
Postmortem report and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 are specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar as a result Sri.Siddappa Nilishettar sustained grievous injury and died due to alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/spot Mahazar, Ex.P4/spot sketch and Ex.P5/offending Vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P-6/IMV Report,
Ex.P-7/Inquest, Ex.P-8/Postmortem Report and Ex.P-9/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at SCCH - 7 13 MVC No.2938/2023 the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar sustained grievous injuries and died in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar noted in the Ex.P8/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 304A of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent citizen Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending Usha Nilishettar vs Nanjundappa on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91915426/
6 vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2 to 4:-

The Learned counsel for the Petitioners has contended that the deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of accident and he was a labourer and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Further the counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 SCCH - 7 14 MVC No.2938/2023 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs of deceased, each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
19.

sentences.text: On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioners claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimants by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioners have not established the income of the deceased, they are not entitled for compensation towards future prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
20. On going through the Ex.P-10 to Ex.P-12 Adhar Cards of the Petitioners respectively it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-10 to Ex.P-12 Adhar cards of the Petitioners it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
21. The petitioners are contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 45 years and he was working as labour and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

The petitioners relied on the Ex.P.8/Postmortem report of the deceased and wherein SCCH - 7 15 MVC No.2938/2023 the age of the deceased is shown as 45 years and this accident was took place on 11.01.2023.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 45 years.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 45 years.
22. It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was working as labourer and earning income Rs.20,000/- p.m.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.15,250/-.

To the aforesaid income, 25% to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.

sentences.text: Thus the monthly income comes to Rs.19,063/- (Rs.15,250/- + 25%).

Since the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses and remaining amount, i.e., Rs.12,709/- (Rs.19,063/- - Rs.6,354/-) has to be taken SCCH - 7 16 MVC No.2938/2023 as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '14'.

Thus the claimants are Usha Nilishettar vs Nanjundappa on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91915426/
7 entitled to compensation of Rs.21,35,112/- (Rs.12,709/- x 12 x 14) on account of loss of dependency.

ORDER

The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Sri. Siddappa Nilishettar noted in the Ex.P8/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 304A of IPC.
